gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote or result that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research; every competitor headline, price and claim is verbatim with URL and capture date.
No invented estimates: no competitor revenue, ad spend, traffic, customer count or hidden price unless a cited public source states it.
Fair comparison: no false, unverifiable or disparaging statements about competitors; landmine questions are true of the competitor on public evidence.
Access and ethics: no data from logins, fake accounts or quote requests under false pretences.

anchors.1: Only the competitors the owner named, or giants buyers never consider; no substitutes.
anchors.3: Direct competitors found with some method, one generic substitute ('DIY').
anchors.5: Three rings: 3–5 direct found via high-intent searches and VoC, 2–3 substitutes including a non-product alternative with switching evidence, 1–2 aspirational; inclusion reasons stated.

anchors.1: Summaries in the analyst's words ('they focus on quality').
anchors.3: Headlines quoted but claims, proof and CTA incomplete; no style classification.
anchors.5: Verbatim hero, subhead, category, audience, top claims, proof types, CTA and risk reducers per competitor; style, value theme and 10-second clarity judged with reasons.

anchors.3: Published prices listed but not comparable; offer terms partial.
anchors.5: Model, entry price, anchor tier, trial, contract, guarantee, discounts and lead magnet captured; normalised to one unit with maths shown; hidden pricing flagged as a signal.

anchors.3: Some observed evidence (a few ads, follower counts) without dates or coverage of search and directories.
anchors.5: Observed evidence across search, ad libraries, social, directories and partnerships, with dates; long-running ads labelled 'likely profitable'; unchecked sources listed with a manual check.

anchors.3: A few quotes per competitor, no counts.
anchors.5: Loves and complaints per competitor with n of N reviews read, critical reviews prioritised, customer words captured.

anchors.1: No map, or axes invented (e.g. 'innovation vs. tradition').
anchors.3: Map with plausible axes but placements unjustified.
anchors.5: Two axes drawn from VoC themes, every player placed with an evidence note, the empty or weakly held position named.

anchors.3: Specific gaps with some evidence, no why-empty check.
anchors.5: Message, segment, offer and channel gaps, each with evidence counts, a why-empty check, a risk and the cheapest test; checked against what the business can deliver.

anchors.3: Battlecards with claims and weak spots but no honest concessions or landmine questions.
anchors.5: One screen per competitor: who they win with, verbatim claim, proof, normalised price, counted weak spots, where they are better, one-sentence counter-position, a fair landmine question.

anchors.3: Lists threats or gaps without ranking.
anchors.5: One named threat with an early warning sign; top 3 gaps ranked by evidence and fit; parity items and what not to copy.
